pr_title: Sonos setup fails with unhandled exceptions on discovery messages
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
During setup of manually configured Sonos devices, if the devices are offline setup of the integration may fail.  There were several issues in the code that needed to be resolved.

1. Exceptions were not being handled when the device was unable to be pinged and were flowing back to HASS during setup.  Now the exceptions are handled and logged, setup will complete, and the devices will be periodically retried.
2. During initialization, a blocking call to soco.uuid was occurring within the HASS event loop, this issue is mitigated by not attempting the ping if the prior call to get the uuid via async_add_executor_job failed.
3. If an exception occurred when pinging the device, the call to async_call_later (to retry it) would not occur and hence the device would never come back on-line without a HASS restart.
4. In the attached issues asyncio.TimeoutError was unhandled, during my testing I saw RequestException occur.  Added these to the existing exception handler to make them consistent.

A question you may have is why I moved the async_dispatcher_send after the ping.   What I found is when I unplugged a speaker that message would get sent and that was keeping the speaker alive beyond the ~270 second timeout so it would not get marked unavailable.   Moving it after a successful ping eliminates that problem at which point that message makes the speaker become available.

review_comments: We probably shouldn’t be patching async_call_later here but that’s an existing issue
Agreed, that's from a prior test.  I'll get that fixed in a new pull request.

This is a change in behavior. The original intention here was to obtain the visible zones from _any_ host and then break. 

That being said, I'm not sure that attempting to detect if any hosts have become unavailable in this manner will be reliable with this method. The call is made to `sync_get_visible_zones` here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/95d16c98293972e3474f27182ac1bd3e50deab7a/homeassistant/components/sonos/helpers.py#L122-L126

The first two attributes return cached values (no I/O attempted) and the last is aggressively cached from the ZoneGroupState, which is shared across all speakers in the system. This means it's very likely that only the first speaker in a loop will actually be tested (and possibly not even that one!).

If you want to actively ensure all speakers are still available, you'd need to make a non-caching call to each device, such as with this method: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/95d16c98293972e3474f27182ac1bd3e50deab7a/homeassistant/components/sonos/speaker.py#L573-L578

Thanks for the helpful feedback and background!

On startup with this scenario, the function was running into trouble.  Assume 3 hosts  listed A,B,C; A+C are on and B is off.  The first call to get visible zones for A succeeds and returns A+C, this causes the top loop to exit.

In the bottom loop, it will loop through A,B,C; when it hits B it determines it is not a known speaker and attempts to send a discovery message, which attempt to access soco.uid which is not known or cached and hence performs a blocking network call which generates an exception related to blocking the event loop which was unhandled and this would then cause setup to fail.

What I think we should try to ensure in the top loop is that we have the info cached. Such that we can exclude hosts in the error list to avoid a) logging lots of messages (prior pull request) and b) avoid event loop blocking calls in the lower loop.

When A,B,C are on, yes we will loop three times at the top, but as you state, all that information comes from cache so it's not a large perf hit.

Certainly the comment could be better.
